# 1.2.96 - one road for numbers, lists, dates and names, one name for every action, option and Call in English and Polish, and 59 rewritten texts the owner approved; players and GMs see new names and new texts

Stage E66 ships alone with this version. 1.2.96 is built on 1.2.95 (E65), which shipped first (01.11.2026) and is
included here; these notes do not repeat it. E66 puts every number, list, date and name a text shows through one road in
the language the page was built in; gives every action, option and Call one name, the same in English and in Polish; calls
the thing a scene leaves behind a Remnant; and lands B01a, 59 of the most-read texts rewritten from what the code does and
approved by the owner (01.11.2026), the model for the texts that follow. **This version changes what players and GMs
read**: names, sentences, counts, dates and the language a window says it is in. It writes one new world setting and adds
no migration; stored world data is not renamed (Before installing). Nothing in this version has been run at a real table
or in Foundry; what was measured was measured headless. 13 commits on top of 1.2.95 (main c014681b), up to
7efb4e58, the last before the release commit; no merges. What was counted and what was not is in Known gaps and Checked.

## Before installing

1. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back.
2. **What changes in a running world.**
   - **One name per action, option and Call, the same in English and in Polish** (the Polish shows the English name; a
     Polish sentence around it declines it, "Remnantu", "Rerolla"). In Title Case and American spelling:
     - Crisis actions: Use an Item, Leave a Clue, Secure a Trace, Self-Defense (was "Self-defence"), Role Reversal, Pin
       Them Down, Keep Your Distance, Finishing Blow, Escape Together, Double Role Reversal, Partners in Crime, Averted
       Eyes, and the crisis action with a weapon, whose Polish label was „Atak bronią”, now by its English name in both
       languages, its last word capitalised. Use an Item's Polish label was „Użyj przedmiotu”; „Zostaw trop”, „Zabezpiecz ślad”, „Ukryj zamiar”,
       „Przygotuj broń” and „Zastaw pułapkę” are gone from `lang/pl.json` as names.
     - The clean-up and the Tamper: **Erase a Trace** (it replaces "Clean up a trace" and "Cover your tracks"; Polish
       „Usuń ślad”, „Zatrzyj ślady”), Misleading Trail (was „Mylny trop”), Move the Body (was „Przenieś ciało”), Reshape a
       Trace; the Indirect Murder's Conceal Your Intent, **Hide the Traces** (it replaces "Cover your traces"), Prepare the
       Weapon, Set the Trap; Observe's Follow My Traces.
     - The Rest options Sleep, Meal and Breath (were „Sen”, „Posiłek”, „Oddech” in Polish); the tile and window
       **Projects** (was „Projekty”, also in the four Daggerheart countdown titles the module sets); **Find Stash** (was
       "Locate a hidden stash", „Znajdź ukrytą skrytkę”); **Find Passage** in Polish too; **Dynamic Action** (was "Dynamic
       action", „Akcja dynamiczna”).
     - **Remnant:** the thing a scene leaves behind is a Remnant in the labels, titles, tabs and column heads in both
       languages (the Investigation tab reads "Remnants" / „Remnanty”; the player handbook's section 8 is "Remnants and
       evidence"). A trace token made from this version on is named "Remnant" in both languages (was "Trace" / „Ślad”).
       "trace" inside longer sentences stays until E71.
     - **Murder Weapon:** English texts that said "crime tool" say Murder Weapon, the item category's name (Polish keeps
       „Narzędzie zbrodni”, the category's own label).
     - **Reroll in Polish:** the Call is Reroll in Polish as in English, verbs included: „Przerzuć” is now „Zrób Reroll”,
       a passive or a statement says the name („Reroll zrobiony”, „Po Rerollu”, „na tym rzucie nie da się już zrobić
       Rerolla”), in 9 values of `lang/pl.json` and on two lines of the Polish GM and player handbooks; no „przerzu”
       is left in either.
     - In Polish also: the Passages tab is „Tajne przejścia”, the passage texts say „tajne przejście” for a passage,
       Testimony and Eclipse are said by their English names, and the debug log's "cleared" line reads "The debug log on
       this browser is now empty." / „Debug log w tej przeglądarce jest teraz pusty.”
     - The six handbooks change by these names alone (220 lines at the rename, ten more lines in English and ten in Polish
       for Remnant in the heads, and the two Polish Reroll lines); no other sentence of theirs is reworded.
   - **59 texts rewritten (batch B01a), approved by the owner:** the hints and descriptions of the actions (Listen's
     and Search's hints left out), the Hope Calls' effects (Determination's left out), the 15 crisis actions' hints, 11
     option hints in an action's own window, and four named texts (the Dynamic Action's two texts, the assignments
     footnote and its setup hint, which now say NPC in Polish). Each was written from facts read in the code that runs
     its rule, in English, and in Polish from the same facts without the new English: 51 written fresh and reviewed in
     English, cold in English, in Polish and against the code, and 8 the owner's approved pilot texts; all 59 approved
     by the owner. They follow a new rule of the style guide, **O19**: a text for a player says only the mechanics a
     player needs - what they do, what it costs and when, what is rolled, what can come of it, and the conditions of
     play that decide it - and never which browser stores or plays a step, that a GM must be connected, or what happens
     when a GM leaves. They are longer on average than the texts they replace.
   - **Strike's miss** no longer promises an Obvious Remnant on a critical failure: a critical is always a success.
   - **Counts agree with their word in both languages.** A text that puts a number before a word that agrees with it
     now picks the right form for every number, where it read "Costs 2 action" or „Kosztuje 2 akcję”
     (in Polish now „Kosztuje 2 akcje. Masz 5 akcji.”, „zostały 2 akcje”, „zostało 5 akcji”); a sentence with two counts
     counts each. 58 keys in each language file that held one string now hold plural forms under the same key.
     - **The crisis hindrance card** read its raw key ("DRPG.Murder.hinderedActions", on a critical
       "DRPG.Murder.blockedActions") after Pin Them Down and Keep Your Distance; it now names the hindered actions and the
       turns ("Their opponent rolls A and B at disadvantage for 2 turns." / „Przeciwnik ma utrudnienie na A i B przez 2
       tury.”; on a critical "Their opponent cannot use A or B for 2 turns." / „Przeciwnik nie może użyć A ani B przez 2
       tury.”).
     - **The price lines:** a cleaner's Tamper whose action step is not needed says so ("No action is needed here. This
       costs 1 Sanity.") instead of "No actions left"; Analyze outside the Class Trial is refused without naming Hope and
       Sanity; a give-back is whispered only when the refund went through.
     - The day summary gives a GM its own first line ("What the table did during the ..."); the trial's start note says
       what the stopwatch does ("The time of day's stopwatch on the HUD starts again from zero when the trial starts, and
       again when it ends.").
   - **Numbers come from the rules, not from the sentence.** A rule's number that a text shows (the crisis actions'
     Sanity and turns, the finishing blow's multiplier, the actions a time of day gives, the Eclipse's crossings, the
     trial's seconds, the Long Rest's cost) is filled from the module's rule tables where the text is made; no rule's
     number changes. One estimate changes with it: the Indirect Murder's budget read "roughly four to six actions" and
     now reads off the rules as 4 to 5 (approved by the owner).
   - **The page's language.**
     - Lists are written by the language: English "A, B, and C" (the Oxford comma) and "A, B, or C", Polish „A, B i C”,
       „A, B lub C” and after a negation „A ani B”.
     - Dates, times and numbers are written in the language the page was built in (the module's Language setting as the
       page loaded), not in Foundry's language or the browser's locale: the case health check's dates, the failure log,
       the messenger's times, a secret's readers, a GM card's "Open until", the evidence log, the notice history's times,
       the room pictures' megabytes, the rooms-per-student ratio and Check rooms' squares ("1,5" on a Polish page). A
       player who changes the Language setting and declines the reload keeps the page's language for every count, list
       and date until the reload (the setting still asks for one).
     - The module's windows (their content and title, not Foundry's frame), the character sheet, the HUD, the notice
       stack, the evidence stage and the module's launchers, tiles and panels carry a `lang` attribute with the page's
       language, so a screen reader reads Polish as Polish. A Polish language file that does not load leaves the page in
       English.
     - Every confirm window of the module says its own Yes and No (Tak / Nie on a Polish page, also over an English
       Foundry): 17 confirms that used Foundry's buttons, approved by the owner on page Q-R3. Three dialogs that carried no
       module class (the case backup, removing another student's item, deleting a table) now carry one.
   - **One new world setting, `documentLanguage`** (the documents' language, D196): world scope, not shown in the
     settings window, empty by default. On the first start of this version the primary GM's browser writes its own page
     language into it, once, and only while it is empty; a second GM joining never writes it. Nothing in this version
     writes a document in it (E57 does). The Language setting is unchanged: the same choices (English, Polski), default,
     scope and reload; its choices are now built from the module's one list of languages. No other setting is added,
     removed or renamed.
   - **No migration, no GM store change, no socket or bridge action.** `migrate.mjs` changes only how one GM whisper
     counts; `gm-stores.mjs` only how its case rows write dates and the backup confirm's class and buttons;
     `gm-bridge.mjs` only how a card writes its "Open until" time; no socket packet, bridge row or guard changed.
   - **Stored world data is not renamed.** The diff has no migration and no write that renames a stored name. Chat cards
     already posted keep the old names. A trace token or row that holds "Trace" or „Ślad” as its name, as builds before
     1.2.96 wrote it, still reads as not described (a finder's copy does not take that word as a name). No language key,
     setting key, flag or identifier is renamed or removed (the 58 keys above keep their names), and the item tables'
     category labels are untouched.
   - `module.json`'s description now ends "In English and Polish (Polski)." It still reads version 1.2.95; the release
     commit sets the version.
   - **The package.** The batch file (`docs/dev/`), the guide, the glossary and `tools/` stay out of module.zip
     (`.gitattributes`); `git archive` lists the same 209 entries at 1.2.95 and at 7efb4e58.
   - **The stage ledger** (`tools/stages.json`): E66's row declares `touches: ["scenes"]` (a Remnant token's name).

## For whoever writes or reviews the module's texts

- **The helpers** (`scripts/utils.mjs`), all on the language the page was built in (`pageLanguage()`, now in
  `settings.mjs` with `LANGUAGES`, the one list of languages): `plural()`, `listOf(items, { type })` with a negated type,
  `localeFormat(kind, value, options)` for `dateTime`, `time` and `number`, `proseOf(entry, field, extra)` for a config
  sentence's numbers (one table, `PROSE_NUMBERS` in `config.mjs`, that `callEffect` reads too, and countable nouns through
  the `DRPG.Unit.*` families), and `worldLocalize(key, data)` for the documents' language, which nothing calls yet.
- **The text lint:** T20 (a locale call outside the helpers, `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, `NumberFormat` and `PluralRules`
  included, with one allowance and its reason) and T28 (the retired names) are FAIL now; T3's baseline is empty. The
  batch file's schema runs T2 on every after, form by form.
- **The batch, `docs/dev/text-batch-B01a.json`.** 59 texts (44 config sentences, 11 window lines, 4 named texts), each with
  its facts (333, 287 read in a named function), the English and Polish before and after, the four reviews, the
  disagreements and the owner's verdict. `node tools/text-render.mjs --batch <file>` renders the owner's sheet.
- **The style guide, `docs/text-style.md`:** O19 in section 2, in the owner's words; the positive model gains B01a's texts
  (B1-B51) and the pilot's pairs 2-8 and 10 at E66; section 14 is the case contract for a fragment inserted into a
  sentence (which Polish case it stands in, which sentences take it); section 13 lists what E66 hands on.
- **The glossary, `docs/glossary.json`:** 118 entries (109 at 1.2.95) and 15 retired names. `truth-bullet` and
  `murder-weapon` are closed; `find-stash`, `dynamic-action` and `self-defense` are new at E66; `neighbor`, `behavior`,
  `recognize`, `favor`, `canceled` and `catalog` are new at stage E71; the `reroll` entry carries the Polish rule.
